RagShortTexts: Montius named men without their offices, leading searchers to arrest namesakes.

Variants.Content: After violence at Gallus’s court, the dying Montius named Epigonius and Eusebius without identifying their offices. Searchers brought in a philosopher and an orator with those names, although the men meant were supervisors of arms production. Fragmentary information caused mistaken arrests; names needed checking against office, location and activity.
A messenger recording only names could draw unrelated people into a prosecution. Identification also required office, place and activity; a shared name proved neither arsenal work nor conspiracy.

An investigator needed to match the arms-supervision office to the persons produced. Fragmentary dying words became an arrest list through violence and transmission, showing the danger of widening liability from incomplete information.
